title: Clyde S NDE 6716
content: I was in the park in Little Rock, checking out the SCA. The SCA is an international organization dedicated to researching and re-creating the arts and skills of pre-seventeenth-century Europe. While watching, I was given the chance to put on knight's armor and a shield, and then wear them in a fight. After about fifteen minutes, I started to get light-headed. I called for a break and started to walk over to the shade (and I might add that it was 110F degrees in the shade). Anyway, after taking about four or five steps, I went down on one knee and stuck the sword into the ground to try to keep myself from falling. It was at this point that I thought to myself, ‘So this is what it's like to die.’ I remember having some regrets that I would be leaving my wife. Then I began to fall over onto my side. In an instant, I was above my body, and then I found myself walking along a path, turning down another path and into a hall, which had lavender fog on both sides and lavender fog about knee deep on the floor. I could see people in the fog on both sides of me, and they were all waving and smiling at me, even though I didn't know any of them. I walked on to the end of the hall and stepped out into a glade that was surrounded by a forest. All of it was lavender-colored. The sky was lavender and the fog was still lavender and swirling around my feet. I was looking around and going, ‘Wow!’ and ‘Far out! This is really cool!’ About that time, I noticed ahead of me an opening in the trees from which a lady emerged and started walking toward me. She was dressed in a lavender gown! I never saw her face, as it was sort of blanked out. Anyway, she came up to me, placed her hand on my forehead, and gently pushed me back down. That is when I woke up, back in my body. There was a doctor who was a member of the SCA working on me. He told me later that I had had no pulse, breathing, or heartbeat for three or four minutes and that I had been dead. I later realized that several years earlier we had buried my adopted mother in a lavender gown. I didn't see anything scary or hellish, and because I was into satanic things at the time, I would have thought that I'd have seen hell or have been tormented by demons or something. As it was, what I saw was all very peaceful and tranquil, and I haven't been afraid of death since. In fact, I look forward to going to the other side. From time to time in recent years, I have seen my home on the other side. I really long to be going home to the mountains and the lake that is there, with my beautiful log home sitting beside the mountain lake. Over the past several years, I have altered my views on religion. I now believe that the God of the Bible that I was brought up to believe in doesn't exist. But the afterlife is what we want it to be and it can be what we make it.

tunnel.passage_other_detail: Walking along a path, turning down another path and into a hall with lavender fog on both sides and knee-deep on the floor.

arrival.other_being_detail: People in the fog on both sides waving and smiling; later a lady in a lavender gown with her face 'blanked out' who placed her hand on his forehead and pushed him back down.

environment.environment_other_detail: A lavender-colored hall with lavender fog; a glade surrounded by a forest; lavender sky; lavender fog swirling around his feet.

context.nde_cause_other_detail: Collapse while wearing knight's armor and fighting in extreme heat (about 110F).

person_demographics.religious_affiliation_detail: Was 'into satanic things' at the time; later rejected belief in the God of the Bible.

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: Hall/path with lavender fog; unknown people waving and smiling; lady in lavender gown touched forehead and pushed him back into body.
stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: OBE above body followed by walking paths/hall, then glade and encounter with a lady, then immediate return.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: Lavender-colored environment throughout; unknown people in fog waving and smiling; a faceless/blanked-out lady in a lavender gown touched his forehead and pushed him back down; later association with adopted mother being buried in a lavender gown; later reports of intermittently seeing 'home on the other side' with mountains, a lake, and a log home.
unique_elements.notable_quotes: “So this is what it's like to die.”; “Wow!”; “Far out! This is really cool!”; “I haven't been afraid of death since. In fact, I look forward to going to the other side.”
